sample_unit: women in a screening mammography cohort

links.outcome: Local calibration (observed-to-expected ratio) of AI risk model versus clinical models in a Mayo Clinic cohort
links.effect: MIRAI overall breast cancer O/E 0.96 (95% CI 0.85-1.08) but invasive cancer O/E 0.68 (95% CI 0.58-0.78), overestimating risk; clinical models O/E 0.86-0.99.
links.quote: MIRAI also overestimated risk of invasive breast cancer across the risk spectrum (observed-to-expected ratio = 0.68, 95% CI = 0.58 to 0.78), whereas clinical models had good calibration (observed-to-expected ratio = 0.86-0.99).

links.outcome: Discrimination versus calibration of AI risk model, including calibration by risk stratum
links.effect: MIRAI C-index 0.71 for overall and invasive cancer, higher than clinical models (0.59-0.68), yet it overestimated risk in low-risk women (about 50%) and for invasive cancer.
links.quote: However, for low-risk women (approximately 50%), MIRAI overestimated risk of overall breast cancer.

screen.reason: Retrospective external validation and calibration assessment of an existing AI mammography risk model (MIRAI) compared against standard clinical risk models on a biobank screening cohort.
